assessment.summary: Release identity, persistent data, runtime secrets, and rollback need one owned boundary before production execution.

assumptions: No measured latency, memory, RPO, or RTO budget was supplied.

opportunities.title: Own the release and secret boundary
opportunities.summary: Separate immutable release artifacts from data, secrets, activation, and recovery.
opportunities.diagnosis: Competing production paths and a mutable live directory disperse ownership of release and credential invariants.

evidence.claim: The alternative deployment path supplies predictable database and JWT fallback values.
The script deletes recorded host identity and synchronizes destructively into the live directory.
Candidate identity, activation, rollback, and persistent-state ownership are not centralized.

desiredInvariants: Every active release maps to one immutable candidate and checksum.
Missing production secrets stop startup without fallback.
Application rollback does not overwrite persistent data or secrets.

options.title: Strengthen current direct-sync scripts
options.summary: Remove unsafe defaults and make checks fatal while preserving the live-directory workflow.

findingCoverage.rationale: Fallbacks are removed but deployment authority remains dispersed.

tradeoffs.assessment: Known defaults and host-key deletion can be removed, but future script drift remains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run configuration failure tests and inspect every production path.
Compare deployment duration and downtime in staging.
Compare service RSS before and after.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fatal checks reduce false success but partial live mutation remains.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject transfer and health failures in staging.

tradeoffs.assessment: The workflow changes little, but recovery remains manual.
The current directory model is preserved.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse the patched script on staging.

workPackages: Remove fallbacks and unsafe SSH behavior
implementationReadiness.rollback: Revert the focused script and configuration changes.

options.title: Versioned atomic Systemd and SQLite releases
options.summary: Promote immutable artifacts through a scoped identity and atomic activation while data and secrets remain external.

findingCoverage.rationale: One canonical production path is selected; fallback removal and possible rotation still remain.

tradeoffs.assessment: Release, secret, data, and activation boundaries become explicit.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Revalidate SEC-003 and test missing-secret startup.

tradeoffs.assessment: Controls run at release time, not on requests.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure deployment duration and request latency before and after.

tradeoffs.assessment: Versioned files consume disk but add no resident service.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure disk retention and service RSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Atomic activation contains partial transfer failure and preserves the previous artifact.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inject failures before and after activation and time rollback.

tradeoffs.assessment: Setup is more complex, but candidate and recovery evidence become repeatable.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Have an operator execute the staging runbook and record ambiguity.

tradeoffs.assessment: Release directories, permissions, service paths, and external state must be introduced.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse transition and reversal without user traffic.

residualRisks: Irreversible database migrations can still block application rollback
Actual credential exposure history remains unknown

implementationReadiness.rollback: Switch the active pointer to the previous verified release; restore data only with separate approval.

opportunities.recommendation: Use atomic Systemd and SQLite releases for Alpha; defer PostgreSQL to a separate post-Alpha migration.
